subject: will anti-correlated features yield anti-correlated beta-weights?

messages.author: 9b1ba46046eac99f
messages.subject: will anti-correlated features yield anti-correlated beta-weights?
parts:
Hi Stan,

inside my model, I have a sampling statement where I use some features to predict choices (= 0 or 1) in an experiment, as shown below:

valfun2 <- beta[3,s] + beta[4,s] * valdiff + beta[5,s] * wgtWith[s,t] + beta[6,s] * wgtAgst[s,t];
chswtch[s,t] ~ bernoulli_logit(valfun2);

The question is that, wgtWith[s,t] always equals to (1 - wgtWith[s,t]), therefore a '-1' correlation coefficient. Yet the beta[5,s] and beta[6,s] (s indicates subject index) is not correlated at all. You may also want to see a pairs() plot of one example subject attached. I wonder, how HMC perceive such situation, and whether beta[5,s] and beta[6,s] would be anti-correlated as well? I also run two other modes where I excluded beta[5,s] or beta[6,s], however, both 'reduced models' make the model performance worse. So at least to me, they provide kind of unique information to the choice data. Is this the right interpretation? Could anybody give me some insights or direct me to some related literature?

Stan model is also attached. I high appreciate any comments!

Lei

> On Monday, May 30, 2016 at 5:56:06 PM UTC+2, Lei Zhang wrote:
> Hi Stan,
>
> inside my model, I have a sampling statement where I use some features to predict choices (= 0 or 1) in an experiment, as shown below:
>
> valfun2 <- beta[3,s] + beta[4,s] * valdiff + beta[5,s] * wgtWith[s,t] + beta[6,s] * wgtAgst[s,t];
> chswtch[s,t] ~ bernoulli_logit(valfun2);
>
> The question is that, wgtWith[s,t] always equals to (1 - wgtWith[s,t]),

Doesn't that mean wgtWith[s,t] is always 0.5? Or was one of those
supposed to be wgtAgst?

Assuming your statement above was a typo and that

wstAgst[s,t] == (1 - wgtWith[s,t])

You can just do the algebra to see what's going on when
you have predictors x and (1-x) and coefficients a and b:

a * x + b * (1 - x) = a * x + b - b * x

In any case, you don't want to have a predictor that's
a linear function of other predictors. And you usually want to
have an intercept. What's happening here is that the b coefficient
is doing the work of a varying intercept. I'd expect a and b here to
be positively or negatively correlated, so i'm not sure what's going
on, which is why I hoped someone better at regression than me
would answer this question.

If I wanted to answer this for myself, I'd do the simulations in
a simpler example than the one you present with just these predictors.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] will anti-correlated features yield anti-correlated beta-weights?
parts:
In any case, you don't want to build non-identifiability into
your likelihood. Practically speaking, you should just drop the
wstAgst parameter that's a linear combo of other predictors.

- Bob
